title: The project states that it has had no security audit and that sandboxing, approval prompts and permission controls reduce risk but do not guarantee isolation

reason: The harness is unaudited, and its sandbox, approvals and permission controls reduce risk but do not guarantee isolation, as upstream says of itself.
justification: Re-examined by debt reviewer K1 after the fix pass: now a scope boundary stated by two records. DH-ADR-SANDBOX-11 (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner) states in its own words that the sandbox, approvals and permission controls reduce risk and are not a guarantee of isolation and that the design has had no security review; it puts that statement in dsh sandbox status, the permissions page, the first-run notice and the website's security page (test DH-T-SANDBOX-17), and makes an independent review a release criterion for the first stable release. DH-ADR-SECURITY-12 states the same and forbids any product text that calls the harness secure without the qualification (test DH-T-SECURITY-1). Neither the audit nor the review can be supplied by a design: the cause is removed only when the review is done, which the gate requires. Note for the coordinator: the two records overlap and name slightly different places for the statement; one should refer to the other.

title: A change to the sandbox policy text shown to the model must be counter-tested with a real model, because an earlier wording made the model stop attempting the tool call in five of twelve runs

reason: Upstream requires a real-model counter-test whenever the model-visible policy text changes, because one wording made a model give up before its first tool call in five of twelve runs. The Go design now has that check: scenario DH-E-SANDBOX-7 runs twelve tasks, six denied first and escalatable, three times on each platform's policy text against a real model, asserts at least one tool call per task and an escalation rate no lower than the previous text's and never below ten of eighteen, and states that a change to the policy text is not merged until it has passed on the new text. The text is produced by the policy resolver of DH-D-SANDBOX-1, whose completion condition includes the scenario. Re-examined by debt reviewer K1; nothing has run.

title: The model menu scenario is skipped on WebKit because WebKit 26.5 crashes while filtering the grouped model rows

reason: Examined by the debt reviewer (K2) after the fix pass. Upstream's debt is a browser test of the model picker switched off for WebKit, so a WebKit defect there would reach users unseen. ui-chat.md now marks step (5) of scenario DH-E-UICHAT-2, the model picker, as engine-sensitive: under owner decision DH-ADR-39 it also runs in current Firefox and Safari, and 'a crash in any engine is recorded as a failed step, never as a skip, and keeps the scenario open'. The picker of DH-D-UICHAT-7 is also filtered on the host, which removes upstream's client-side filtering of grouped rows. What is resolved is the skipped check; whether WebKit renders the picker correctly is what the scenario will show when it runs.

title: About 150 lines of per-file coverage exclusions in the test configuration, six of them marked TODO (client test lane, inspector, web worker)
evidence: vitest.config.ts:275-430; vitest.config.ts:288; vitest.config.ts:330; vitest.config.ts:346; vitest.config.ts:355; vitest.config.ts:388; vitest.config.ts:424

reason: The exclusion list exists because the per-file 100% rule cannot be met where V8 coverage cannot see child processes or browser code. DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-7 replaces the rule with one uniform package floor measured across processes, with exclusions by rule only and never by a list of files, so there is no list to keep or to work off. The inventory missed the six markers because the file is at the repository root, outside its scan roots, and three of them sit in the middle of a comment line.

title: The hosted serial macOS reference job is disabled with `if: false` and a TODO to re-enable it before release

reason: Upstream's main-branch workflow carries a switched-off macOS job. In the Go design macOS is one of three operating systems of the required harness job (DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-12), and the acceptance workflow fails when a listed scenario skips or does not run (DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-6), so a platform lane cannot be absent without a failing job. The inventory missed the marker because workflow files are outside its scan roots.

title: Whole packages are excluded from the test run on Windows by a list in the test configuration: the bash shells, the three hook packages, the bash terminal, the local sandbox, SSH and most subprocess suites

reason: Upstream keeps one list of packages whose tests never run on Windows, so a Windows defect in them is found by a user. The toolchain specification changes this (section 3, the row for vitest.config.ts:24-64): a file that cannot run on an operating system carries a build constraint next to the code, the required harness job runs on Linux, Windows and macOS (DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-12), and a listed scenario that does not run fails the job (DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-6). The areas concerned state their Windows behaviour themselves (PowerShell executors, the Windows sandbox backend, a Windows local end for SSH, hook scripts in PowerShell).

title: The time limit of a model-written program is an unfinished design: whether a wait for approval uses up the budget, whether a total lifetime backstop is needed, and which processor and memory limits of the process tree can be enforced

reason: The Go design answers each open question of the note. A tool call's budget counts execution time only and pauses while a nested call waits for approval (DH-D-TOOLS-3, test DH-T-TOOLS-8). A workflow run has a wall-time budget counted by the host, which keeps running while a nested call waits for a person and says so as its tradeoff, plus a memory and a process-count limit carried out by the tree owner and reported as enforced, partial or unavailable (DH-ADR-PTC-5). No processor meter is added, which the same decision states.

title: The live test of search through the vendor's server-side web search tool is disabled because the live endpoint can finish without structured source blocks

reason: Upstream switched off its live test of the model-backed search provider because an answer can arrive with no structured sources. The Go design defines that case: DH-D-CONNECT-11 returns such an answer as a query result with zero sources and the flag unsourced, its text labelled "answer without sources" so the model is told not to cite it, never inventing a source, and logs a warning after three in a row (test DH-T-CONNECT-24). Its real-vendor scenario DH-E-CONNECT-8 expects both kinds of answer and asserts each is handled, instead of assuming sources, so the live check need not be switched off. The selection and no-fallback rules are those of DH-ADR-CONNECT-8. Re-examined by debt reviewer K1; nothing has run. The fact that the endpoint may send no source remains, and is reported, not hidden.
